label: Matthew-Mark Cross-Translation Validation
description: Standing validation collection: Matthew+Mark subtexts from the Douay-Rheims (1582-1610) and the 1599 Geneva Bible. Cross-translation ground truth for all Palimpsest similarity/masking validation.
copyright_note: Source text bodies are copyrighted-edition scripture (DR 2018 reprint / Geneva Tolle Lege 2013). Per repo convention (imports/ gitignored; no reference.txt committed) the bodies are NOT committed. Regenerate locally from imports/ with build.py; assert with validate.py.
parity_note: Geneva 1749 vs DR 1747 verses (+1 Matthew, +1 Mark) reflects genuine Vulgate-vs-Protestant versification differences — intended cross-translation variance, not an error.

companion_collections.label: Matthew / Mark — 6-way cross-translation
companion_collections.description: Matthew-only and Mark-only single-book subtexts from all three translations (DR, 1599 Geneva, KJV). The collection the corpus-graph over-merge / score-gate, phyletic tree, and synoptic precision/recall oracle are validated against. Each member is a derive-of-a-derive (split from the *-MM subtext), so building it also exercises derivation robustness.
companion_collections.kjv_note:
The KJV EPUB packs a whole chapter into one

with inline N markers; kjv-complete verse-paragraph-patches it (

before each verse span) so paragraph-vs-paragraph alignment is not degenerate. The KJV layout is a Mt+Mk+Lk superset so the Luke outgroup stays re-derivable.

companion_collections.label: Matthew / Mark / Luke (7-way, Luke outgroup)
companion_collections.description: The six 6-way members plus a KJV Luke single-book subtext as a genuine phyletic outgroup (none of the same-book Matthew/Mark texts is a true root). Used to stress-test the phyletic tree.
